label: text
content: not an official compilation like the other Shih-lu, but apparently a private one. Nothing is known about the author and the date of compilation. There exists only one ancient manuscript copy, now in the possession of the Academia Sinica, Taiwan. A photographic reprint is included in the 1940 edition of the Ming shih-lu. The Shih-lu for the first four moons of the reign of the Ch'ung-chen emperor, 9th moon to 12th moon T'ien-ch'i 7, are in the 1940 edition attached to the Hsi-tsung shih-lu (No. 1.1.13).

label: text
content: ## 1.2 The Huang Ming t'ung-chi, its editions and supplements

label: text
content: ## 1.2.1 Huang Ming t'ung-chi 皇明通紀 (1555)

label: text
content: Number of chuan varies, by Ch'en Chien 陈建 (1497-1567, 1528 cj.) from Tung-kuan 東莞, Kuangtung: 89-Index, III, 201a; 東莞縣志, 1926 edition, 58, 6a-9a. History for the period from the beginning of the dynasty, 1351, to the end of Cheng-te, 1521. It was the first comprehensive history of the Ming dynasty at that time. According to the author's preface he was persuaded by a friend to write a chronicle of the Ming, since at that time no such work did exist. Ch'en Chien's work must thus have been one of the most popular histories of the Ming dynasty. But soon after its publication it was severely criticized for misleading statements and for an alleged distortion of the historical truth. As early as during the Lung-ch'ing period the censor Li Kuei-ho 李貴和 proposed the burning of the printing blocks of the T'ung-chi and got the emperor's consent. But apparently this order had only a limited effect. The book was soon reprinted and became all the more popular; it is even quoted quite often in the T'u-shu chi-ch'eng. It has been suggested that the book was not written by Ch'en Chien but by Liang I 梁億 (1511 cs.) from Shun-te 順德, Kuangtung, younger brother of Liang Ch'u 梁儲 (1451-1527, 1478 cs. 89-Index, II, 182b); 順德縣志, edition 1853, 23, 37a. During the Ch'ing period the T'ung-chi, including all new editions and supplements, was listed for suppression. Preface by the author 1555. No copies of the original edition are known. But there is a large number of later editions and supplements still extant. Probably there are even more than listed below.

label: text
content: REF.: CCT,4,11a；明史藝文志,p.33；TSS,p.229b；ARJ,III,311；Shen Te-fu沈德符，野獲編 (see No.4.1.5)25,pp.638-639.

label: text

label: text
content: (24h) 14 chüan by Pu Shih-ch'ang卜世昌(late Ming) from Hsiu-shui秀水, Chekiang. These 14 chüan comprise the work by Ch'en Chien. A supplement covering the Chia-ching period to 1566 was added by Pu Ta-yu卜大有(1547 cs.) from Hsiu-shui, (89-Index, II, 2a) and edited by Pu Shih-ch'ang with the title Huang Ming hsü-chi皇明續紀 in 3 chüan. A further supplement is the Huang Ming t'ung-chi shu-i皇明通紀述遺 by Pu Shih-ch'ang in 12 chüan. Chüan1-11 contain additions and supplements to the two previous works, chüan12 covers the Lung-ch'ing period to 1572. The latter has prefaces by Feng Meng-chen 馮夢顔, 1605; by T'u Lung屠隆, and by Pu Wan-ch'i卜萬誄, 1605. Printed at the聚奎堂.

label: text
content: (24k) 11 chiian. Probably a reprint of the last-mentioned edition with another division. Chiian 1-9 are the original work by Ch'en Chien, chi'an 10-11 cover the Chia-ching and Lung-ch'in periods to 1572. Although Pu Ta-yu卜大有 is not mentioned as the author of the supplement, the text has the same additional notes by Chih Ta-lun支大綸 and Wu Jui-teng 呉瑞登. The preface by Ch'en Chien is dated 1586 (?). In an inner page, the work has the title Huang Ming tzu-chih t'ung-chi ta-ch'iun皇明資治通紀大全. Reprint (重梓) of 1608.

content: ## 1.2.6 Huang Ming t'ung-chi ts'ung-hsin lu 皇明通紀從信錄 (1627)

label: text
content: (24b) 40 chüan by Shen Kuo-yuan 沈國元 (飛仲), from Wu-hsien 吴縣, Kiangsu. Chüan 1-27 are a revised edition of Ch'en Chien's Huang Ming t'ung-chi (No. 1.2.1) with commentary and marginal notes; chüan 28-40 cover the Chia-ching, Lung-ch'ing, and Wan-li periods from 1522 to 1620 with a few commentaries and marginal notes. Preface 1620. A supplement under the title Liang-ch'ao ts'ung-hsin lu 兩朝從信錄 in 35 chüan by the same author covers the T'ai-ch'ang and T'ien-ch'i periods from 1620 to 1627. Prefaces by Ch'en I-tien 陳懿典 and by the author. Both works

label: text
content: prohibited; original edition only. Shen's work is said to be the most valuable edition and in particular the most valuable supplement of the Huang Ming t'ung-chi.

label: text
content: REF.: CCT, 4, 12a; TRD, VIII, 481 (erroneously mixes up both titles); TSS, p. 229b; Hsieh Kuo-chen, 1, 16b-18a and 4, 18b-20b; ARJ, III, 310.

content: ## 1.2.7 Huang Ming shih-liu-ch'ao kuang-hui chi 皇明十六朝廣彙記 (1632)

label: text
content: 28 chiuan by Wang Hsiang 王襄 (a private scholar of the late Ming/early Ch'ing period) from An-fu 安福, Kiangsi: 安福縣志,1872 edition,11,25a-b; and by Ch'en Lung-k'o 陳龍可 (1622 cs.) from Chin-chiang 晉江,Fukien: see No.1.2.8.

label: text
content: Chuan 1-11 are a revised edition of Ch'en Chien's Huang Ming t'ung-chi (see No.1.2.1) covering the period from the beginning of the dynasty to the end of Hung-chih (1505). Chuan 12-28 cover the time down to 1627. Almost half of the whole work (chuan 19-28) covers the seven years of T'ien-ch'i (1621-27) only. The events on the Liao-tung border during this time are dealt with in particular detail. Corrected (較) by Ch'iu Yu 丘酉. Prefaces by Wang Hsiang, Li K'ang-hsien李康先, and Tsou Te-yung 鄒德泳, all dated 1632; by Ch'iu Yu, 1631. Printed at the Yu-shih-chu 友石居.

content: ## 1.2.8 Huang Ming t'ung-chi chi-lu 皇明通紀幃錄 (Ch'ung-chen period)

label: text
content: 27 chüan by Ch'en Lung-k'o 陳龍可 (1622 cs.) from Chin-chiang 晉江, Fukien: 晉江縣志, edition 1765, 11, 62a.

label: text
content: Chüan 1-15 are a new edition of Ch'en Chien's Huang Ming t'ung-chi 皇明通紀 (No.1.2.1) with commentary and marginal notes by Ch'iu Chün 丘瀚, covering the time from the beginning of the dynasty to the end of Cheng-te (1521). Chüan 16 by Ch'en Lung-k'o, edited (鑒定) by Ch'en Tzu-chuang 陳子壯 covers the first 22 years of Chia-ching to 1543. Chüan 17-24 by Ch'en Lung-k'o, edited (鑒定) by Ch'iu Erh-ku 丘爾穀, cover the period from Chia-ching 23 (1544) to the end of T'ien-ch'i 2 (1622). Chüan 25-27 without the name of the author or editor given, cover the years T'ien-ch'i 3-7 (1623-1627). The appendix, Wen-kuan p'in-chih yüeh-feng 文官品職月俸 lists the ranks and salaries of civil officials. Preface by Ch'en Jen-hsi 陳仁錫; printed at 吳門五車樓.

label: text
content: The authenticity of the authors and editors of this work seems to be rather questionable. The well-known Ch'iu Chun died as early as Hung-chih 8 (1495)

label: text
content: and could not be the editor of a historical work going down to 1521 and even to 1543. There may, however, be another person of the same name living in the seventeenth century.

content: ## 1.3.1 Hsien-chang lu 憲章錄 (1573)

content: (27) 46 chiuan by Hsueh Ying-ch'i 薛應旂 (b.1500,1535 cs.) from Wu-chin 武進, Kiangsu: 89-Index, 11, 201c.

label: text
content: - The 89-Index has mixed up two different people by the same name. Our author had the fancy-name Ming-chü 明舉 and the biography in 國朝列卿紀110,5a refers to him. The other one had the fancy-name Hsi-lun 羲輪 and was from Wu-chiang 吳江, Kiangsu. He lived during the T'ien-chi-i-period and is mentioned in CCT,27,7b as the author of the P'o-weng-chi 破甕集. The biographical note in 明詩綜 67,16b refers to him. The two Huang Kuang-sheng are not mentioned in the古今同姓名大辭典.
